comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Reopened, and the earlier dismissal was too quick.** Prompted by the question "this is all virtual, there's *gotta* be a way" - which is right. Two ways, and they are not equally good.

**The render shim - ask for a right split, draw it on the left - does not survive contact.** Attractive because it needs no second round trip. It fails on keying: the tree arrives fresh from the daemon on every `layout_updated` and every reconnect, so "this node is mirrored" has to be Muster's own fact, stored, and re-applied to each incoming tree. A split node has no id to store it against. This codebase already answered why - `SetSplitRatio` addresses a divider by the turns down to it precisely because "a divider is not a thing a backend hands out an id for, it is a position in a shape that changes under it". A path shifts whenever anything above it splits or closes, and a mirrored flag that follows the wrong node is a pane that silently swaps sides.

Three more costs, once the lie is permanent rather than momentary:

- **Resize inverts.** `ResizePane` names a pane and a direction and is resolved by the daemon against *its* rects, which are unmirrored - it is the one intent Muster explicitly cannot compute for itself. Under a mirrored node, "grow this pane leftward" moves the wrong divider. Correctable by counting mirrored ancestors on the axis, which is more logic riding on the keying that does not work.
- **Two clients disagree.** herdr is multi-client and `herdr --session muster` is the documented escape hatch. A herdr TUI on the same session would show the panes the other way round, permanently, for a project whose durability story is that the daemon owns the truth.
- **Ratios invert too**, so every drag has to know which orientation it is looking at.

**Rearranging is the answer, and the flash is solvable by not rendering the intermediate.** `corpus/herdr-0.8.0/split-sides/` already records that the pair works: `swap_changed: true`, settled shape `right(w1:p2, w1:p1@0.5)` - exactly what a leftward split should produce. The defect is only that both arrangements reach the client, 100.4 ms apart.

So: issue `pane.split`, issue `pane.swap`, withhold that tab's layout in between, and apply the settled tree the swap answers with. Afterwards Muster and the daemon agree completely - no stored annotation, no keying problem, resize works, other clients see the same thing.

**What this card previously called "a new power in the mirror" is less new than it read.** A shell already understands "this tab's tree is being withheld": `View::of` withholds a layout that disagrees with the tab's panes, and the doc comment there says withholding is a state the shell already has the right answer to - it leaves what it is showing alone. What is genuinely new is that this withholding is *intentional and tied to an in-flight intent* rather than derived, so it needs a timeout and a decision about failure. Both are small:

- **Timeout or refusal → apply whatever the daemon last said.** The user gets a pane on the side they did not ask for, which is exactly today's behaviour minus the chord existing. It degrades to correct-but-unasked-for, never to a lie.
- **Watch `invalid_pane_swap`** (recorded in observations section 14): a swap naming no target raises rather than refusing, and it arrives *after* a split that already succeeded - so a caller treating it as a plain failure has made a pane it never undoes.

**Cost to the user: about 100 ms before the new pane appears.** For an operation that is spawning a shell anyway, that is not perceptible as a delay - and it is strictly better than 100 ms of a pane sitting in the wrong place and then jumping, which is what the current measurement describes.

The upstream ask stays worth making, because a four-way `SplitDirection` would make all of this unnecessary. But it is no longer the only path, and Muster should not wait on it for two chords a Ghostty user has in their fingers.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
**Landed.** All four sides split, and the two herdr has no request for cost about a millisecond more than the two it does.

The 100.4 ms this card was built around was never the price of the pair - it is the gap between two *broadcasts*, and the recording measures both clocks now: the pair answers in 15.3 ms, of which `pane.swap` is 1.5, and `PaneSwapResult` carries the whole settled arrangement. Muster was throwing that answer away and waiting to be told the same thing again.

So: the adapter issues the pair and hands back what the daemon said, the mirror applies it, and the broadcast it overtook is dropped once. No timeout and no clock - an arrangement is only suppressed while the daemon still owes a broadcast of it, and each entry is spent on its first match.

Three things the real app caught that the corpus did not:

- **A swap moves daemon focus to the source pane**, so the arrangement published between the halves differs from the settled one in its cursor as well as its shape. Whole-layout equality let the flash straight through; suppression names the arrangement instead. Recorded in observations 14.
- **Arming whatever the mirror held before was too broad.** Closing a pane collapses a tab back to a shape it held earlier, and that broadcast is the only thing saying the pane is gone - suppressing it left a dead square nothing could dismiss.
- **The keyboard did not follow a split.** Pre-existing and racy in all four directions; deterministic here because settling from the answer publishes before the pane event lands. Fixed the way tabs already did it - a pane Muster made is *wanted* until the daemon describes it.

Ghostty ships `split_left` and `split_up` unbound, so Muster does too: the actions are in the menu and one `[keymap]` line from a chord.

The upstream ask is unchanged and now purely an economy - a four-way `SplitDirection` would delete the second request, the reconstruction and half the suppression. It rides on a_26BJbJeZL.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
herdr's `SplitDirection` is `right` and `down`, and a split always puts the new pane on the `second` side. So a four-way splitting keymap - which is what people arrive from Ghostty expecting, and what a real config binds - has no direct request behind it. Two of the four chords do nothing in Muster today.

Building it out of `pane.split` + `pane.swap` was measured rather than assumed, and it is not good enough. Both arrangements get published, **100.4 ms apart**: the new pane appears on the right, sits there for six frames at 60fps, then jumps left. Muster renders what the daemon says, so that is a flash a person sees, in a project whose premise is native feel.

**The ask:** a four-way `SplitDirection`, or a split that names which side the new pane lands on.

**What Muster could do alone, and why it is not doing it yet:** hold a tab's layout updates between issuing the split and the swap returning, then apply the settled layout `pane.swap` already answers with. That is a new power in the mirror - suppressing published truth while an intent is in flight - and it interacts with reconciliation. Not worth taking on for two chords while an upstream answer is plausible.

Also recorded on the way: a `pane.swap` naming no target raises `invalid_pane_swap` rather than returning one of its four refusal reasons, and it would arrive *after* a split that already succeeded - so a caller treating it as a plain failure leaves a pane it never undoes.

Evidence: `corpus/herdr-0.8.0/split-sides/`, `docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md` section 14.
title: 🪓 Upstream: there is no splitting leftward, and faking it flashes
